In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of an organisational form for a technological collaboration is the result of a complex process, in which different factors are considered.

the choice of an external technology acquisition mode is a complex and multifaceted process, in which the decision maker has to take into account several factors, both of a technological and of an organisational nature.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a technology sourcing decision can be considered as a process which involves three phases: (1) identification and evaluation of the technology to be acquired; (2) identification of the potential partners; and (3) selection of the most appropriate sourcing strategy.

the choice of the organisational mode for external sourcing of technological innovation is a complex process, where the selection is not based on a few simple and clear-cut criteria, but rather on a set of factors that have to be evaluated in a dynamic way.

a company has to choose a sourcing strategy by evaluating the following aspects: the degree of innovation and the degree of risk of the project to be developed; the degree of uncertainty and the degree of complexity of the project to develop; the degree of appropriability and the degree of imitability of the technology to be developed; and the degree of compatibility of the technology to develop and the degree of complementarity of the technology with other technologies in the company portfolio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
companies tend to consider the technological collaboration as a whole, and that they do not focus on a single aspect of the technological collaboration.

, while the choice of a sourcing strategy depends on a number of factors, the most relevant are the nature of the innovation (radical or incremental), the degree of uncertainty, the level of risk and the level of technological competence of the company.

, while the decision process is not linear, the decision maker is not completely free in the selection of the organisational mode: the choice is made within a set of alternatives which can be reduced to a limited number of options.
